about: Field notes the Agronomy Advisor may attach to a job. Every note is general farm practice written by the team, NOT taken from a cited source, so every note is advice only (verified: false). Same rule as the weather playbook: no source, no action. To let a note carry weight, add a source[] with title, publisher, url and dateRead, have a person check it, and set verified: true.

notes.text: {soil} holds water and packs down under wheels when wet. Have someone check the ground carries the machine before it goes in.
{soil} drains and dries fast. Moisture for seed or after irrigation does not last long here.
This is among the lowest ground on the farm ({elevation} m on a coarse elevation model). Water from rain or irrigation collects on low ground first.
The product label sets the rate, wind limits, buffer distances and how long people stay out afterwards. Check it for this field and crop before the first pass.
Tilling works best when the soil crumbles in the hand: not sticky, not dusty.
Seeding depth and rate for {crop} come from the seed supplier. Check the seeder is set for them before the first pass.
Cut {crop} needs dry days to cure before baling. Ask the Weather Manager about rain before cutting.
Tree rows and low branches: this field needs slower travel and more clearance than open ground.
The survey gives this ground a {slope}% slope. Spray and irrigation water can run off downhill.

topics.irrigation: Irrigation is not scheduled by this team. What it knows: each field's soil and drainage class from the USDA soil survey, and the soil-moisture reading the weather feed carries.
topics.fertiliser: Fertiliser rates are not held by this team. They come from a soil test and the crop plan; a person sets them.
topics.pests: Pest and disease scouting is not done by this team. A spray job is the response; the product label and a licensed applicator decide the product and rate.
topics.harvest: Harvest timing is a person's call. The team can bring a harvest job forward when the Weather Manager asks, and the Plan Manager decides.
topics.planting: Planting dates and varieties are a person's call. The team seeds the fields the operator lists and reports soil facts for each.
topics.livestock: This farm plan has no livestock work. The team runs field jobs only: spray, mow, till and seed.
topics.soil: Soil facts come from the USDA NRCS soil survey (SSURGO) at each field's map position: map unit, drainage class and slope.
topics.labour: People's work at the depot (fuelling, implement changes, inspections) is the Depot Manager's. Only a person can mark it done.
